measured.unit: distinct (function, halting-time) pairs with exponential maximum halting time, of 493 pairs over 4096 machines

caveats: Verdict follows the pre-registered rule literally and should be read as 'refutes as operationalised'. Every census number the book reports is reproduced: 748 machines never halt, 3348 sometimes, 1683 always; 149 total functions; 230 total (function, time) pairs; 17 machines compute x+1; machines 378, 1953, 2289 are exactly the exponential-time machines computing total functions; and all eleven example formulas (5, 6n+3, 4n+3, 2n+3, 2n^2+8n+7, 2^(n+2)-3, 2n+1, 3, 2n+1, 4n-1, ~2.5n^2) are matched exactly. The only count differences are 352 vs 351 partial functions and 493 vs 492 pairs.

Criterion (a) failed because 49 of 493 pairs are classed 'other' by the pre-registered fits, and 56 of the 61 machines involved remain 'other' when extended to inputs of length 14. None of these is cubic or super-exponential: their T(n) alternate with the parity of n (e.g. 7, 19, 15, 27, 23, 35, 31, 43, ...) or settle after a transient, and a parity-aware fit classes 45 as linear, 6 as constant and 3 as quadratic exactly, leaving two machines (2242, 2439) with quadratic growth modulated with period 4. The book's statement about growth rates is therefore supported in substance; the pre-registered fit tolerance (relative RMS 0.15 on n = 3..10) was too strict for bounded oscillations around a linear trend.

Criterion (b) failed under the pre-registered reading that 'the same function' means agreement on all of x = 0..1023 including where a machine does not halt: the three exponential pairs computing total functions (378 with 1351, 1953, 2289) have 261-269 constant-time partners each, exactly as the book says, but the three pairs computing partial functions (924 and 2142, each undefined on one input x = 0 or x = 1 and computing x with its lowest bit cleared; 3626 with 3717, undefined on x = 0 and computing the identity) have only linear-time machines computing the same partial function. If 'same function' is read on the halting domain only, each of these has 261-269 machines producing the same outputs in a single step, and the book's statement about all six exponential cases holds.

The extended run used a cutoff of 2^17 instead of the pre-registered 2^20 steps because the vectorised runner's memory grows with the cutoff; the longest halting time observed among the extended machines is 303, so the reduced cutoff could only matter if a machine with sub-quadratic times up to n = 10 jumped above 131072 steps between n = 11 and 14.

Part 1 (sets): for length n = 3, enumerate all 764 involutions of the 8 strings and all 256 subsets S; for n = 4, take 300 pseudo-random involutions of the 16 strings (numpy seed 20261031, including the complement map, reversal and the identity-on-some-strings cases) and all 65536 subsets. For each (involution, S) record complete, consistent, |S| versus half. Part 2 (multiway systems): enumerate all multiway systems over {A,B} with one or two rules lhs -> rhs, |lhs| in {1,2}, |rhs| in {|lhs|, |lhs|+1} (length-non-decreasing so that the set of generated strings of each length <= 6 stabilises and can be computed exactly), started from the string 'A' taken to represent true; for each system and each length n = 2..6 record the exactly generated set, under negation = complement and under negation = reversal. PASS (supports) if in Part 1 and Part 2 there is no counterexample to either direction of the biconditional (complete and consistent <=> exactly half) for any involution.

measured.unit: stabilised (multiway system, length, negation) cases that generate exactly half of the strings but are not complete and consistent

caveats: The three implications the book actually argues (more than half => inconsistent; less than half => incomplete; hence complete and consistent => exactly half) hold without exception in every enumerated case, for every length-preserving involution including those with fixed points.

The converse that makes 'exactly half' a criterion (exactly half => complete and consistent) is false: it fails for 3.94 million of the enumerated (involution, set) pairs and for 80 stabilised cases among the 1485 small multiway systems, e.g. {A -> BB, BB -> AA} from A generates exactly half of the length-6 strings while being both inconsistent and incomplete. The criterion is therefore necessary but not sufficient; it becomes sufficient only if consistency (or completeness) is known independently.

For any negation with fixed points (e.g. reversal, where palindromes are their own negation) no set is complete and consistent at all (0 of 65536 sets at length 4; 0 of the 659 fixed-point involutions at length 3 admit one), so the 'exactly half' count carries no information about completeness and consistency in that case.

The multiway enumeration is restricted to length-non-decreasing rules so that 'eventually generated' is exactly computable; this restriction excludes systems whose generated sets at a given length never stabilise, but the counterexamples found are exact.

info.hypothesis: Among the simplest equational axiom systems for one binary operator (single equations with at most four operator occurrences), the large majority admit several non-isomorphic finite models (operator forms) on 2 and 3 elements, and only a small minority force a single form.
info.pass: Pre-registered. Family: all single-equation axiom systems lhs == rhs where lhs and rhs are terms built from one binary operator and variables, with a total of n = 1..4 operator occurrences in the equation, variables named canonically in order of first occurrence (a, b, c, ...) reading lhs then rhs, excluding equations with lhs identical to rhs, and identifying an equation with its side-swapped twin (so each unordered pair of sides is counted once). For each axiom system and each k in {2, 3}, enumerate all k^(k^2) operator tables (16 and 19,683), keep those satisfying the equation for every assignment of the variables, and count the models up to isomorphism (relabelling of the k elements by any permutation): m2 and m3. Definitions: 'many forms' = m3 >= 3; 'single form' = m2 <= 1 and m3 <= 1 and m2 + m3 >= 1; 'no non-trivial form' = m2 = m3 = 0 (only the one-element model). The claim PASSES if the fraction of axiom systems with 'many forms' is >= 0.80 and the fraction with 'single form' is <= 0.05. Reported, not decisive: the same fractions restricted to n = 4; the list of 'single form' systems; the systems whose k = 2 model set is exactly {Nand, Nor} (operators 7 and 1 in Wolfram's numbering) or {Xor, Xnor} (6 and 9); and, as a validation of the model-finding code against the note 'Properties of operators from axioms' (p. 1171), the k = 2 model sets of all lhs == a systems with up to 6 operators under this canonical labelling, listing how many allow only {6, 9} and only {1, 7} (the note reports 32,004 and 964 for its family of 274,499 systems; the family definition in the note is not fully specified, so this is a plausibility check, not a decisive comparison).

measured.unit: fraction of axiom systems with >= 3 non-isomorphic 3-element models ('many forms')

caveats: Pre-registered decision: 40.5% of the 4692 simplest single-equation axiom systems have 'many forms' (>= 3 non-isomorphic 3-element models), below the pre-registered 50% failure bound, so the 'vast majority' reading fails in this family; the 'single form' fraction (14.5%) falls in the mixed band (5-20%). The verdict follows the pre-registration, but the confidence is low because the result is sensitive to definitional choices listed below.

32.5% of the systems (1525) have no 2- or 3-element model at all (e.g. a o b == c, a o (b o c) == b o (a o c) == ... forcing a one-element structure); whether such degenerate equations belong to the population Wolfram had in mind is unclear. Excluding them, and adding a capped 4-element search (supplementary S2: 306 further systems gain >= 3 forms at k = 4; 1703 searches hit the node budget, so this is a lower bound), the many-forms fraction is 52.0% and the single-form fraction 6.4%, i.e. the mixed band rather than failure.

In Wolfram's own illustrated family (lhs == a with lhs over {a, b}, up to 3 operators; supplementary S1, 101 systems), 67 (66%) allow >= 3 forms for some k <= 4, 4 force a single form and 4 have no non-trivial form, which is closer to his description but still short of 'vast majority' at the 80% reading. The pre-registered validation against the note on p. 1171 was uninformative: under this canonical labelling no lhs == a system with <= 6 operators has k = 2 models exactly {Xor, Xnor} or {Nand, Nor}, because the note's family evidently uses a different variable convention (its counts 32,004 and 964 could not be reproduced).

Only models with 2 and 3 elements (and a capped 4-element search) were examined; the pictures in the book go to 4 elements exactly. Isomorphism is relabelling of elements only (duality/anti-isomorphism not identified). Thresholds (80% / 50%, 5% / 20%) are readings of 'vast majority' and 'only a few'. Six systems have exactly {Nand, Nor} as 2-element models, e.g. ((a o b) o (b o (a o a))) == b, consistent with the book's statement that short axioms for Nand exist, and 40 have exactly {Xor, Xnor}.

info.hypothesis: If the claim holds, the published six-Nand single axiom ((a.b).c).(a.((a.c).a)) = c has exactly the models that Nand-logic has on small domains (on 2 elements only Nand and Nor, on 3 elements none, on 4 elements only the 12 operation tables isomorphic to the Nand of the four-element Boolean algebra); no shorter single axiom of the form X = variable passes even the 2- and 3-element screens; and in a natural enumeration of axiom systems by number of Nands a system passing all screens appears within the first few thousand.
info.pass: Pre-registered. Enumerate all Nand expression trees X with k Nands (k+1 leaves) over variables a, b, c and consider (I) single axioms {X = a} for k <= 6 (34488 systems for k <= 5, 288684 for k = 6, plus the 16896 two-variable systems for k = 6) and (II) two-axiom systems {X = a, a.b = b.a} with k = 4 (3402 systems, 6 Nands in total). Screen each system against all 16 binary operations on {0,1}, all 19683 on {0,1,2} and, by backtracking search, all operations on {0,1,2,3}; a system 'works up to n values' if its models on each domain of size <= n are exactly the operation tables isomorphic to the Nand (or, on 2 elements, Nand or Nor) of a Boolean algebra of that size, i.e. {Nand, Nor} on 2, none on 3, the 12 tables isomorphic to Nand_4 on 4. PASS (supports) if (a) the published axiom works up to 4 values; (b) no single axiom {X = a} with k <= 5 over <= 3 variables works up to 3 values; (c) at least one system of family (II) works up to 4 values, and the number of systems of forms (I) and (II) with at most 6 Nands in total that precede it in the enumeration (fewer Nands first) is below 10000. The book's counts (0 of 16896 two-variable six-Nand systems up to 3 values; 296 of 288684 up to 3 values and 100 up to 4 values; 32 of 3402 in family II) are recorded as cross-checks and do not decide the verdict. If the 4-value search over all 3-value survivors of (I) exceeds 20 minutes it is applied only to the published axiom and to family (II), and the 100-count cross-check is dropped and reported.

measured.unit: six-Nand three-variable single axioms {X = a} (of 288684) whose models on domains of size 2, 3 and 4 are exactly those of Boolean Nand

caveats: Criterion (a) holds: the published six-Nand axiom has no 3-element model and exactly the 12 Boolean-Nand models on 4 elements, and every count the book reports for its search (0 of 16896, 296 of 288684, 100 up to 4 values, 32 of 3402) is reproduced exactly.

Criterion (b) as pre-registered fails: 8 four-Nand and 16 five-Nand single axioms over three variables survive the 2- and 3-valued screens (e.g. ((b.a).(a.(b.c))) = a). All 24 fail on 4 elements (they admit non-Boolean 4-element models), so none is an axiom for logic; the pre-registered 3-valued screen was too weak to separate 'passes a screen' from 'is as short as possible'. Under the 4-valued screen six Nands is indeed the smallest size with any survivor among single axioms {X = a}.

Criterion (c) fails only on the count bound, and only because the pre-registered enumeration order places every single axiom with fewer Nands before the two-axiom family: the first family-II system that works up to 4 values is number 1248 of the 3402 family-II systems with 6 Nands (number 1716 counting family-II systems of all sizes), but up to 36204 when all 34956 shorter single axioms are counted first. Whether that is 'the first few thousand' depends on the order chosen; the book's own text counts only the family it searches.

Finite-model screening is necessary but not sufficient for axiomatising Boolean algebra; the sufficiency of the published axiom (that it proves all of Boolean algebra) rests on the equational proof the book reports and was not re-derived here. Per the pre-registered rule, (a) true with (b) and (c) failing as described gives 'mixed'; every failure is a calibration artefact of the pre-registered criteria rather than a disagreement with the book's reported search results.

nodes.label: nand-axiom-enumeration-generator
neutral_substitution_rate

info.english:
**Kimura (1968).** Under neutral Wright–Fisher evolution, the substitution rate equals
the mutation rate, for every population size `M`.
kernelChecked: A neutral absorbing chain on {0..M} copies (stochastic, mean-preserving, both ends absorbing, positive one-step escape from every interior state) fixes a mutant with probability i/M, with an explicit geometric error bound at every finite time t.
The Wright-Fisher binomial kernel is such a chain (row sums, mean preservation and absorption proved from Bernstein polynomial identities).
With u = 1/M the defined substitution rate M * mu * u equals mu, also in the diploid 2N form and as the t -> infinity limit.
assumed: Strict neutrality of the mutations.
Constant population size and Wright-Fisher reproduction (non-overlapping generations, multinomial sampling).

Independent fates of mutants: the substitution rate is DEFINED, as in Kimura 1968, as (new mutants per generation) x (fixation probability of one mutant). Interference between lineages is excluded by that definition, not proved absent.
The mutation rate mu per copy per generation is a free parameter; nothing here measures it.

prov.file: lean/Delphi/Kimura.lean

nodes.label: NeutralChain.fixedBy_tendsto

info.english:
**Neutral fixation probability (Kimura 1962, neutral case).** A neutral lineage that
starts with `i` of `M` copies is eventually fixed with probability `i / M`.
kernelChecked: Fixation probability i/M for any neutral absorbing chain, hence for the exact finite Wright-Fisher chain (Delphi.NeutralChain.fixedBy_tendsto).
assumed: Neutral case only (s = 0). Kimura 1962 with selection in the diffusion limit is not formalised.

prov.file: lean/Delphi/Kimura.lean

nodes.label: fisher_fundamental_theorem

info.english:
**Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection** (haploid locus, partial change).
The change in mean fitness over one generation of selection, with fitnesses held fixed, equals
the variance in fitness divided by the mean fitness.
kernelChecked: For one locus with finitely many types, frequencies p (nonneg, summing to 1), fixed fitnesses w and mean fitness > 0: selection p_next = p w / wbar yields wbar_next - wbar = Var(w)/wbar exactly.
Corollary: mean fitness never decreases under fixed fitnesses.
assumed: Haploid or clonal inheritance, so the variance in fitness IS the additive genetic variance; the diploid average-effect version is not formalised.
Fitnesses constant within the step (partial change): no dominance, epistasis, frequency dependence or environmental change.
Infinite population: deterministic frequencies, no drift, no mutation.

prov.file: lean/Delphi/Fisher.lean

nodes.label: twofold_cost_of_sex

info.english:
**Twofold cost of sex.** With equal fecundity and a `1 : 1` sex ratio, the odds of asexual to
sexual females double every generation. Fecundity cancels.
kernelChecked: For 0 < q < 1 and fecundity f > 0 the odds of asexual to sexual females satisfy odds(q_next) = 2 odds(q), and f cancels.
Iterated n generations the odds are 2^n times the initial odds.
assumed: Anisogamy: males contribute nothing to offspring number or survival.
Equal fecundity and viability of sexual and asexual females and of their daughters.
Primary sex ratio exactly 1:1 in sexual broods; discrete non-overlapping generations; infinite population (deterministic fractions).

prov.file: lean/Delphi/MaynardSmith.lean

nodes.label: FavoredChain.fixationProbability_ge

info.english:
**Lower bound on fixation when selection does not oppose the mutant.** A lineage starting from
`i` of `M` copies in a favored chain is eventually fixed with probability at least `i / M`.
kernelChecked: For any absorbing chain on {0..M} copies with E[X_{t+1} | X_t = i] >= i (stochastic, both ends absorbing, positive one-step escape from every interior state), P(fixed by t) is nondecreasing and bounded, its limit u(i) exists, and u(i) >= i/M (Delphi.FavoredChain.fixationProbability_ge); also u(i) <= 1.
Wright-Fisher sampling with success probability (1+s) i / (M + s i), s >= 0, is such a chain (Delphi.wrightFisherSelection), so a single new mutant fixes with probability at least 1/M.
The defined expected count M mu u T equals mu T for the neutral Wright-Fisher chain, is at least mu T for any favored chain, and is at most M mu T for any u <= 1.
assumed: The expected count is a DEFINITION (rate x generations, independent fates, Kimura 1968); linkage, interference, changing M, changing s and overlapping generations are excluded by it, not shown absent.
Selection enters only through the sampling probability (1+s) i / (M + s i), constant in time and across sites.
mu, T, M are free parameters; the module measures nothing. Which mutations are favored, how many a trait needs, and in what order, are outside it.

nodes.label: C1: the long-run rate at which neutral mutations become substitu

info.english: the long-run rate at which neutral mutations become substitutions, relative to the mutation rate
kernelChecked: A neutral absorbing chain on {0..M} copies (stochastic, mean-preserving, both ends absorbing, positive one-step escape from every interior state) fixes a mutant with probability i/M, with an explicit geometric error bound at every finite time t.
The Wright-Fisher binomial kernel is such a chain (row sums, mean preservation and absorption proved from Bernstein polynomial identities).
With u = 1/M the defined substitution rate M * mu * u equals mu, also in the diploid 2N form and as the t -> infinity limit.
assumed: Strict neutrality of the mutations.
Constant population size and Wright-Fisher reproduction (non-overlapping generations, multinomial sampling).

Independent fates of mutants: the substitution rate is DEFINED, as in Kimura 1968, as (new mutants per generation) x (fixation probability of one mutant). Interference between lineages is excluded by that definition, not proved absent.
The mutation rate mu per copy per generation is a free parameter; nothing here measures it.

nodes.label: C1b: whether neutral substitution rates can differ between lineag

info.english: whether neutral substitution rates can differ between lineages that share a mutation rate (for example through population size)
kernelChecked: A neutral absorbing chain on {0..M} copies (stochastic, mean-preserving, both ends absorbing, positive one-step escape from every interior state) fixes a mutant with probability i/M, with an explicit geometric error bound at every finite time t.
The Wright-Fisher binomial kernel is such a chain (row sums, mean preservation and absorption proved from Bernstein polynomial identities).
With u = 1/M the defined substitution rate M * mu * u equals mu, also in the diploid 2N form and as the t -> infinity limit.
assumed: Strict neutrality of the mutations.
Constant population size and Wright-Fisher reproduction (non-overlapping generations, multinomial sampling).

Independent fates of mutants: the substitution rate is DEFINED, as in Kimura 1968, as (new mutants per generation) x (fixation probability of one mutant). Interference between lineages is excluded by that definition, not proved absent.
The mutation rate mu per copy per generation is a free parameter; nothing here measures it.

nodes.label: C4c: whether mean fitness can change under selection when the var

info.english: whether mean fitness can change under selection when the variance in fitness is zero
kernelChecked: For one locus with finitely many types, frequencies p (nonneg, summing to 1), fixed fitnesses w and mean fitness > 0: selection p_next = p w / wbar yields wbar_next - wbar = Var(w)/wbar exactly.
Corollary: mean fitness never decreases under fixed fitnesses.
assumed: Haploid or clonal inheritance, so the variance in fitness IS the additive genetic variance; the diploid average-effect version is not formalised.
Fitnesses constant within the step (partial change): no dominance, epistasis, frequency dependence or environmental change.
Infinite population: deterministic frequencies, no drift, no mutation.

nodes.label: C3: the fixation probability of a single new mutant that selecti

info.english: the fixation probability of a single new mutant that selection does not oppose
kernelChecked: For any absorbing chain on {0..M} copies with E[X_{t+1} | X_t = i] >= i (stochastic, both ends absorbing, positive one-step escape from every interior state), P(fixed by t) is nondecreasing and bounded, its limit u(i) exists, and u(i) >= i/M (Delphi.FavoredChain.fixationProbability_ge); also u(i) <= 1.
Wright-Fisher sampling with success probability (1+s) i / (M + s i), s >= 0, is such a chain (Delphi.wrightFisherSelection), so a single new mutant fixes with probability at least 1/M.
The defined expected count M mu u T equals mu T for the neutral Wright-Fisher chain, is at least mu T for any favored chain, and is at most M mu T for any u <= 1.
assumed: The expected count is a DEFINITION (rate x generations, independent fates, Kimura 1968); linkage, interference, changing M, changing s and overlapping generations are excluded by it, not shown absent.
Selection enters only through the sampling probability (1+s) i / (M + s i), constant in time and across sites.
mu, T, M are free parameters; the module measures nothing. Which mutations are favored, how many a trait needs, and in what order, are outside it.

R9b: with AreaLaw F instead, σ_b(L2)/σ_b(L1) = 1, log exponent 0 (bendingStress_ratio_sheet, bendingStress_log_sheet): no size limit follows.

Constant σ_max; static loads only (wind on a leaf is outside the model); which load family applies (R9a or R9b) is empirical and must be committed by the candidate.
